- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending up.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially after recent spikes; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to early forecast.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +1.5–2.0% above peak or use moving average smoothing.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >72, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes; if <68, add 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Sentiment + price spike → model delays correction; if sentiment turns positive after spike, forecast should accelerate upward.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; use 3-day moving average of recent prices to anchor forecast.
